key_provisions_or_claims: Experiment with 227 participants and four anthropomorphism levels supports an uncanny valley of perceived trustworthiness.
Medium anthropomorphism lowers use intention via reduced intuitive and deliberate perceived trustworthiness.
At high (human-indistinguishable) anthropomorphism, only intuitive perceived trustworthiness determined use intention.
Anthropomorphic design has both advantages and pitfalls for social robot acceptance.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper reporting an experiment (227 participants, four anthropomorphism levels) testing an uncanny valley of perceived trustworthiness for social robots through dual-processing theory. Medium anthropomorphism reduces use intention via both intuitive and deliberate trust; at near-human levels only intuitive trust matters. No governance content; design implications for acceptance.
annotation.title_clean: Between Anthropomorphism, Trust, and the Uncanny Valley: a Dual-Processing Perspective on Perceived Trustworthiness and Its Mediating Effects on Use Intentions of Social Robots
annotation.title_en: Between Anthropomorphism, Trust, and the Uncanny Valley: a Dual-Processing Perspective on Perceived Trustworthiness and Its Mediating Effects on Use Intentions of Social Robots
annotation.venue: Proceedings of the 54th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS)
